When we built Make Me Rap — a browser studio that turns a user's photo, theme, outfit, scene, and voice choice into a full 768p lip-synced rap music video — we chose a split Cloudflare architecture: a Cloudflare Worker (running React / Next.js App Router on Vite) backed by D1 and private R2 buckets for all auth, checkout, and state transitions, paired with a dedicated Cloudflare Container render coordinator that claims paid jobs and orchestrates long-running video generation.

articles.title: Your MCP tool middleware can't return a 429
articles.excerpt: A reader of my book on MCP servers asked a fair question: why isn't the companion code built on mcp-go? So I ported it. The protocol part was easy. The interesting part was finding out which checks ca…
articles.body: A reader of my book on MCP servers asked a fair question: why isn't the companion code built on mcp-go ? So I ported it. The protocol part was easy. The interesting part was finding out which checks can't live where an SDK invites you to put them. The short version: anything whose answer is an HTTP status code has to run before the SDK sees the request. That includes the 401 that starts OAuth discovery, the 403 that names the missing scope, and the 429 with Retry-After . Tool middleware is too late for all three. The experiment mcp-go (v1.6.0, MCP revision 2026-07-28 ) gives you server.WithToolHandlerMiddleware . It wraps every tool call, and it's the obvious place for a rate limiter: type ToolHandlerFunc func ( ctx context . Context , request mcp . CallToolRequest ) ( * mcp .

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .

articles.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner.''
articles.body: Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve.
